text:
ian: FYI - noticed a recurring pattern: small bursty tenants (mostly realtime-search and interactive-embed jobs) are thrashing HBM slabs on us-west2. that leads to preemptions of fractional slices and noisy-kv-cache churn. thinking we should try a short experiment: a tiny dedicated pool for high-bandwidth tenants + scheduler soft-isolation (reduce spillback) + route hedging off hot racks. any objections?

penny: can you share the slab eviction metrics and tenant list? need to see which tenants are truly high-bandwidth vs just long-running.

omar: link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/slab-evictions?from=now-6h&to=now - spikes line up with t-realtime and t-embeds during 09:00-11:00 UTC. preempt_count for fractional tenants up 2.4x.

ops-bot: ALERT: us-west2 slab_evictions > 300/min (10m avg) - trigger THROTTLE-7223

zara: quick idea - rather than big dedicated carveout (expensive), create a micro-dedicated pool: 2x full GPUs reserved and pinned to tenants with a history of >75% sustained HBM. This keeps most noisy traffic off shared slabs but is cheap. fallback routing to us-west1 if pool saturates.

ian: agreed on micro-pool. also propose scheduler tweak: introduce `spillback_penalty` for tenants flagged as high-bandwidth (0.7 default), which reduces their chance to be placed on fractional slices.

penny: cost check? 2 GPUs reserved in region ~ $5.5k/mo amortized + added cross-region routing on overflow maybe +$300-700/mo. Also ops overhead for tagging tenants.

omar: implementation steps: 1) build tenant classifier (simple rules + recent HBM/p95) 2) tag tenants `high_bw=true` 3) create pool `micro-dedicated-usw2` with 2 cards 4) scheduler: prefer pool for `high_bw` tenants and set `spillback_penalty=0.7` 5) route overflow to us-west1 with hedged weights.

zara: we should also reduce eviction aggressiveness for tenants moved into pool to avoid thrashing during migration; set `slab_guard=soft` for those tenants for 30m after migration.

ian: commands (canary):
```
# create micro dedicated pool
fleetctl pool create --name=micro-dedicated-usw2 --region=us-west2 --cards=2 --labels=purpose:noise-mitigation
# tag tenants using classifier (dry-run listed)
tenantctl tag --file=classify-highbw.csv --dry-run
# enable soft-isolation in scheduler for high_bw tenants
schedulerctl set-tenant-flag --tenant-selector 'label:high_bw' --flag spillback_penalty=0.7 --flag slab_guard=soft --ttl=30m
# route overflow to us-west1
routingctl set-weight --from=us-west2 --to=us-west1 --tenant-selector 'label:high_bw' --weight=0.25
```

penny: +1 but add telemetry: capture tenant-level p50/p95, slab_eviction_rate, preempt_count, and inter-region egress. Need alert if p50 latency increases > baseline + 25%.

omar: also add a placement check: ensure micro-pool cards don't share PCIe root with hot shared hosts. use existing `pcie_root_id` tags if present or run a quick `lspci` probe.

zara: good call. small script: `fleetctl node-probe --nodes micro-dedicated-usw2 --probe=lspci-root` and fail pool creation if both cards map to same root.

ian: timeline: canary create micro-pool tonight 02:00 UTC; tag 2 tenants as `high_bw` (dry-run then live) at 03:00 UTC; route overflow + slab_guard tweak at 04:00 UTC; monitor for 8h. who wants pager?

penny: I'll be pager for the first 4h. omar backup. notify #incidents if slab_evictions don't fall by 20% or p50 regresses.

sre-bot: CHANGE-7223 created by ian - micro-pool canary scheduled 2026-04-02T02:00:00Z. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/micro-dedicated-pool-playbook.

omar: one more thought - if micro-pool saturates often, we should consider a low-latency pre-emption window: allow the micro-pool to borrow ephemeral fractional slots in the same rack for short bursts with guaranteed quick fallback. That reduces overflow egress but is more complex. keep as phase-2.

zara: agreed. phase-1 focus on isolation + tagging + routing hedging. phase-2 design doc later.

ian: I'll create the change and post run results here. keep experiment cheap and short (2 weeks). :thumbsup:
